To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

during short circuit of series-connected IGTs, the dv/dt depends on the gate drive unit and the gate current, and that the Miller capacitance determines the dv/dt in the case of a low gate current, whereas the plasma capacitance is relevant in case of a high gate current.
the dv/dt during a short circuit is determined via the plasma-capacitance or via the Miller-capacity, depending on the gate drive unit and the gate current.
the dv/dt depends on the gate drive unit and the gate current and that the dv/dts are different for short-circuit type-2 and 3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behavior of series connected IGBTs during short-circuit.
the short circuit behavior of IGBTs and the voltage balancing of series-connected IGTs.
a better understanding of the short-circuit behavior of the IGBT and the design of gate-drive units.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dv/dt of series-connected IGBTS is not only dependent on the plasma capacitance but also on the gate current, which is controlled by the Miller capacitance, and the gate resistance.
the dv/dt during short circuit is determined either by the plasma capacitance or by the Miller capacitance, but not by a mixture of both.
the dv/dt depends on the gate-drive circuit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dv/dt during short-circuit type two and three can be controlled by a suitable gate-drive.
the short-circuit behavior is not only determined by the device characteristics but also by the gate-drive unit.
the dv/dt during short-circuit type-2 and 3 depends on the gate current and the plasma-capacitance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gate drive unit can be designed such that the IGBTs are operated in a stable manner during short-circuit type-2, and that the dv/dt can be limited to 10 kV/μs.
the gate-drive unit has a significant influence on the short-circuit behavior and therefore on the short-circuited current.
the gate current has a strong influence on the desaturation behavior of series-connected power semiconductors.
